<frame id="90:18" name="Pointly Case Study 2" x="3044" y="-13771" width="1440" height="10571">
  <frame id="413:70" name="What I Learned Section" x="426" y="9646" width="918" height="643">
    <text id="413:8" name="What I Learned" x="428" y="9681" width="845" height="44" />
    <rounded-rectangle id="413:9" name="Conclusion Rectangle" x="426" y="9752" width="894" height="537" />

    <line id="413:11" name="Line 72" x="426" y="9646" width="892" height="0.00007798112346790731" />
    <text id="413:12" name="Different experiences can reveal shared needs. Interviewing travelers with varying levels of points experience taught me to look beyond individual preferences and use common patterns to guide product priorities.  AI helped me build faster, but I still had to decide what was worth building. At the hackathon, I turned our interview findings into a PRD and used AI coding tools to build a working prototype. Testing it with users helped me see where those decisions worked and where they needed refinement.  The process reinforced two lessons: making information available is only useful if people can easily understand and act on it, and an established visual palette helps multiple designers create one cohesive experience." x="735" y="9824" width="492" height="397" />
  </frame>

    <text id="413:14" name="From Research to MVP Prototype" x="426" y="8170" width="845" height="24" />
    <text id="413:15" name="We designed the experience to help travelers decide how to use their points. Our high-fidelity MVP prototype brought rewards balances, personalized stays, and points-versus-cash comparisons together to support more informed booking decisions. The project remained at the prototype stage." x="426" y="8209" width="856" height="78" />

    <text id="138:95" name="Insight" x="499" y="3726" width="845" height="105" />
    <text id="138:94" name="Users did not necessarily need more ways to earn points. They needed help understanding the value already sitting in their wallets." x="735" y="3726" width="535" height="140" />

  <frame id="413:75" name="Interviews + Interview Tiles" x="322" y="2561" width="998" height="1087">

    <text id="136:44" name="Different travelers.  A shared need for clarity" x="428" y="2605" width="845" height="82" />
    <text id="137:3" name="I interviewed 10 travelers to understand how they managed rewards, evaluated redemption value, and navigated decisions around transfers and group travel." x="428" y="2713" width="865" height="57" />

    <rounded-rectangle id="136:57" name="Thoughtful interview with laptop-1 1" x="426" y="2956" width="284" height="190" />
    <text id="136:61" name="“The bank portals feel like Expedia from 2010. It’s hard to know if I’m getting a good deal.”" x="465" y="2852" width="207" height="96" />
    <text id="136:81" name="“I want to plan trips with friends, but it’s so hard to coordinate and share options together.”" x="1072" y="2852" width="215" height="189" />

  <frame id="413:54" name="Challlenge Section" x="120" y="1789" width="1200" height="381">
    <text id="90:28" name="Groups can’t pool rewards Friends may have significant rewards collectively, but few tools show what becomes possible when their points are considered together." x="736" y="2089" width="584" height="81" />
    <text id="90:27" name="Finding the best redemption requires expertise Comparing cash, points, transfer partners, and booking portals means navigating different values, rules, and systems." x="736" y="1988" width="584" height="81" />
    <text id="90:26" name="Scattered rewards Travelers accumulate points across credit cards, airlines, and hotels without a clear view of what they can unlock together." x="736" y="1887" width="584" height="81" />
    <text id="123:17" name="Point.ly began as a startup concept from a United Airlines manager who wanted to give travelers one view of their rewards. Travelers face three problems:" x="734" y="1789" width="586" height="78" />
    <text id="90:20" name="The Challenge" x="120" y="1789" width="472" height="76" />
  </frame>

    <rounded-rectangle id="348:6" name="Points Box" x="426" y="5585" width="439" height="249" />
    <text id="145:138" name="Savvy travelers knew the transfer partners and redemption tricks. Everyone else had the same options but no easy way to find them. " x="1000" y="5679" width="296" height="91" />
    <text id="348:11" name="Instead of a flat “not enough points,” provide a list of creative ways to close the gap, such as current promos and affiliated points programs. " x="1000" y="5944" width="269" height="91" />
    <text id="348:15" name="For people planning together, looking at combined resources rather than individual balances could open travel options" x="545" y="5944" width="269" height="91" />
    <text id="348:7" name="Knowing you have 80,000 points is meaningless unless you know what they can buy and whether transferring is worth it. " x="543" y="5684" width="281" height="91" />
    <text id="348:5" name="Insight: Expertise created  an uneven playing field" x="1000" y="5621" width="296" height="48" />

    <text id="348:16" name="Opportunity: Suggest ways to pool rewards for group travel" x="545" y="5886" width="296" height="48" />
